good.text: My bedroom has a door, a bed, and a cabinet. I have achieved everything my ancestors dreamed of.
I counted the engravings on my bedroom wall twice. Both times the answer was magnificent.
Slept in my own room last night. Nobody hauled a corpse past my bed. Pure luxury.
My bedroom is so fine the elves would weep. Good. Let them weep.
A smoothed floor, a real bed, and a chest just for my socks. Finally, dignity.
I gave my bedroom a name. It is called Mine, and nobody else may enter.

bad.text: My bedroom is a hole. Not a cozy hole. A hole the miners forgot about.
There is no door on my bedroom, so the cat simply walks in and judges me.
I sleep in the dormitory next to Urist, who snores like a collapsing tunnel.
My room is so small my beard has to wait out in the corridor.
Rough walls, dirt floor, and a bed clearly made by an apprentice. Disgraceful.
The noble down the hall has four rooms. I have a closet with ambitions.

good.text: I finished a job today and nobody interrupted me to haul a stone. A historic first.
Work is going wonderfully. I have not cancelled a single task all week.
Put in a full shift, and my hands still remember what they are for.
No feeling finer than a finished task with a mug of ale waiting at the end.
My work order came through, the materials were there, and the workshop was not on fire.
I did my job so well the overseer nodded at me. Nearly nodded, anyway.

bad.text: I was assigned hauling again. I have hauled more rocks than the river has.
Cancelled my job three times. Item inaccessible, they say. It was right there!
Somebody put my workshop beside the refuse pile. I will be filing a grudge.
Worked all day and achieved nothing but a sore back and a fresh hatred of stairs.
They pulled me off my trade to carry barrels. Barrels! I am an artist.
My tools went missing, and I suspect the cat. Or worse, a noble.

good.text: Nothing happened today and honestly it was lovely. I stared at a wall for hours.
No goblins, no beasts, no tantrums. I could get used to dull.
I had no job, so I watched the plump helmets grow. Thrilling, in its way.
Idle time is just thinking time. I thought about ale, mostly.
Quiet days are rare in a fortress. I spent this one counting my socks.
Being bored means nobody is on fire. That is a good day by fortress standards.

bad.text: I have been on break so long I forgot what my hands are for.
The fortress is too quiet. Something must be about to eat us.
I am so bored I volunteered to clean the dining hall. Twice.
No work, no fights, no news. I may start a strange mood just for something to do.
I counted the stones in the meeting hall. There are not enough to count again.
If nothing happens soon, I will dig a hole just to see what comes out.

good.text: Had a proper chat with a friend today. We complained about elves for an hour.
Being alone is fine, really. My pick never interrupts me.
Spent the evening with friends in the tavern and nobody threw a single mug.
Somebody remembered my name today, and not even to assign me hauling.
I am never lonely. I have a cat, a beard, and a grudge against the mayor.
Caught up with an old friend by the well. We agreed the sky is still too big.

bad.text: I have not spoken to anyone in a season. Even the cat ignores me.
I tried talking to a statue. It was a good listener, but rather cold.
I miss my companions. The fortress is full, but my table is empty.
I waved at someone in the corridor. They were busy hauling a corpse past.
Nobody sits with me at dinner. I eat my plump helmets in silence.
I wrote a letter to a friend, then remembered I cannot write. Lonely and illiterate.

good.text: I finally did the thing I needed to do, and my soul unclenched like a fist.
Got that need met at last. I feel like a freshly cut gem.
Scratched an itch I have had since the last migrant wave. Wonderful.
My needs are seen to. The fortress is not a total failure after all.
Satisfied a craving I did not even know I had. Now I am unstoppable.
I took care of myself today. Even dwarves need a little upkeep, like hinges.

bad.text: Something is missing in my life, and it is not just ale. Though it is also ale.
I have needs. Nobody in this fortress has asked about them once.
I feel distracted, unfocused, and faintly furious at the masonry.
There is a hole in my heart, and the miners swear they did not dig it.
My needs have gone unmet so long they have started filing complaints with the mayor.
I cannot concentrate. Something is wrong, and it might be everything.

good.text: I drank something from the cavern and now I can hear colors. Ten out of ten.
I feel euphoric. I may have licked a mushroom. I regret nothing.
Whatever was in that barrel made me feel like a hero of legend.
My vision is sparkly and my toes are warm. Is this what elves feel like?
I ate something glowing. My beard is now slightly brighter. An improvement.
I am floating, though my feet insist otherwise. Excellent mug of something.

bad.text: I ate something off the cave floor and my stomach has opinions about it.
I feel sick. I suspect the ale was actually some creature's blood.
My skin itches and I can taste the number seven. Not ideal.
I drank from the wrong barrel. The wrong barrel was full of regret.
Something bit me in the caverns, and now my arm is the wrong color.
I am dizzy, queasy, and I keep seeing a carp that is not there.

good.text: I am improving every day. Soon they will carve my face into a wall.
Learned something new today. My hands are smarter than my head now.
A little better every day. At this rate I will be legendary before the next siege.
I practiced until it clicked. Then I practiced more, purely out of spite.
My skill went up, so I celebrated with a mug and a short, dignified jig.
The apprentices watch me work now. I pretend not to notice. I notice.

bad.text: I got better at something, but it was hauling. Nobody wants to be good at hauling.
I improved, yet the elves still sing better than I work. Infuriating.
I am learning, but slowly, like water seeping through granite.
They say I am improving. They also said the dam would hold.
I leveled up and my reward is more work. Typical fortress economics.
My master calls me adequate. Adequate! I will show him adequate.

good.text: There is a smell in the hall, but honestly it reminds me of home.
The rot stench means somebody has been busy. I respect industry.
I have smelled worse. The miasma and I have reached an understanding.
A little miasma keeps the elves away. Every cloud has a purple lining.
My nose has gone completely numb from the smell, which is oddly restful.
It stinks down there, sure, but I found a sock in it. My sock!

bad.text: Something is rotting near the dining hall, and it is not the plump helmets.
The miasma is so thick I could carve it. Nobody will let me.
I walked past the corpse pile and now my beard smells of regret.
Who leaves a goblin to rot by the stairs? Haul your corpses, people!
The smell followed me into my bedroom. It is on my pillow now.
I breathed purple air today. A dwarf should not see their breath that color.

good.text: The goblin is dead. I would say rest in peace, but he never cared for peace.
Saw the beast's corpse. Good riddance. It ate my favorite mug.
Death is part of fortress life. So is lunch. Today I chose lunch.
They buried old Urist with full honors. Lovely slab, very good engraving.
I have seen so many bodies I am calm about it now. Losing is fun, they say.
A fine funeral, and someone even brought ale. The deceased would approve.

bad.text: I saw a corpse in the hallway, and nobody has moved it in a week.
Another one gone. I will carve their name, if anyone ever gives me a slab.
My friend died and the fortress just kept hauling. Does nobody ever stop?
I stepped over a body on the way to breakfast. Breakfast was ruined.
There are more coffins than beds now. I have checked, twice.
Death is everywhere and the dining hall is right next to the tombs. Planning!

good.text: I felt rain today and it was refreshing. Like a bath that falls on you.
The sky leaked on me and I did not hate it. Do not print that.
The rain washed the blood off my boots. Very considerate of the weather.
Water from the sky, free of charge. The outdoors has exactly one good idea.
I stood in the rain and pretended I was a waterfall. Nobody saw. Probably.
The rain smells of moss and wet stone. Practically underground, really.

bad.text: I was rained on. Rained on! Water belongs in wells, not on my head.
My beard is soaked through and smells like a wet cat.
Who designed weather? The sky drips on everyone with no warning whatsoever.
It rained and my socks got wet. My socks! The good ones!
Got drenched hauling logs. Elves would call that romantic. I call it soggy.
It rained on me this {season}. I demand a roof over the entire world.

good.text: I went outside and the sky did not swallow me. Practically a holiday.
The sun was out and so was I. We tolerated each other nicely.
I have grown used to the open air. I only screamed once today.
Saw a cloud shaped like an anvil. The sky is finally learning.
Being outdoors is fine, provided you keep one eye on the trees.
Fresh air is overrated, but I admit it beat the miasma.

bad.text: The sky is too big. Someone should dig it a ceiling.
I was outside for an hour and felt like a pebble on a dinner plate.
The sun stared at me the entire time. Rude, and very bright.
I have lived underground so long that daylight feels like a personal insult.
No walls, no roof, no comfort. Outside is just a cave that gave up.
There is far too much up out there. Up should have a limit.

good.text: Had a mug of ale so good I briefly forgave the elves.
Fresh dwarven wine! I could hug the brewer. I will not, but I could.
A proper drink in a proper mug. All is right under the mountain.
I drank something truly fine today. It tasted of victory and barley.
The ale is flowing, and so are my compliments to the brewer.
One mug for me, one mug for my beard. Both of us are happy.

bad.text: No ale! I had to drink water like some kind of elf.
The stockpile is dry. I have been sober for a worrying number of hours.
Someone brewed with rotten plump helmets. I am not saying who. It was Urist.
I drank plain water today. Plain water. I feel like a fish.
The barrels are empty and the brewer is on hauling duty. Madness!
My mug is dry, and so, I warn you, is my sense of humor.

good.text: Had a lavish meal. I may compose a poem about the roast.
The cook outdid himself. That biscuit had layers. Actual layers.
Plump helmet stew again, and somehow it was better this time.
I ate something prepared by a real chef and wept into my beard.
Fine meal, finer company, and nobody fed me carp. Perfect evening.
The food was so good I asked for seconds and got them. Unheard of.

bad.text: Raw plump helmets again. I am starting to look like one.
I ate a meal so bland the elves could have cooked it.
There is nothing in the food stockpile but seeds and sadness.
The cook used a rat. I know because it still had its tail.
I am hungry. The kitchen has been about to cook since last season.
I ate cave moss for breakfast. It tasted like a dark, damp tunnel.

good.text: The dining hall has engraved walls now. I eat like a baron.
Ate in a truly grand dining room. My soup had never felt so respected.
There is a statue in the dining hall. It watches me eat, approvingly.
Real tables, real chairs, real atmosphere. Somebody actually planned this one.
The dining room is so fine I lingered over my mug for an hour.
They smoothed the dining hall floor. My dinner no longer rolls away.

bad.text: I ate my dinner on the floor beside a dead goblin. Not ideal.
The dining room is just a corridor with a table in it.
No chairs! I had to eat standing up, like some kind of horse.
The dining hall smells of the refuse pile next door, and so does my soup.
Somebody built the dining hall next to the butcher. I have lost my appetite.
Rough stone walls, a wobbly table, and apprentice mugs. Dreadful dining.

good.text: Slept like a stone. A happy stone, in a lovely bed.
I had a full night's rest and woke up ready to strike the earth.
Dreamt of a mountain made of gold and ale. Woke up refreshed.
Best sleep in years. Nobody woke me up for a siege.
Proper bed, proper blanket, proper snore. I am a new dwarf.
I slept so deeply the miners thought I had been quarried.

bad.text: I slept on the floor again. The floor and I are not friends.
Woken by noise from the workshop. Who smelts at midnight?
Could not sleep. The sky was in my dreams, being enormous.
I have been so tired I nearly napped inside a barrel.
Slept in the dirt like a goblin. My back will never forgive me.
Somebody was hammering all night. I hope it was important. It was not.

good.text: Spent some quiet time with {deity} today. We understand each other.
I prayed to {deity} and felt warm all over. Could have been the magma.
A good long prayer to {deity}. My soul is polished like a gem.
{deity} heard me, I am sure of it. A rock fell, and it missed.
I visited the temple and {deity} did not disapprove. Big day for me.
Prayed until my knees ached. {deity} is worth every sore knee.

bad.text: I have not prayed in ages. {deity} must think I moved to an elf forest.
There is no temple in this fortress. I prayed in a broom closet.
I tried to pray to {deity}, but someone kept hauling bins through the shrine.
{deity} has been silent. I have been silent too. We are both sulking.
I feel distant from {deity}. Probably the lack of a proper temple.
I knelt to pray and a cat demanded my attention instead. Typical.

good.text: Had a great argument about mugs today. I won, obviously.
I comforted a friend today. Then they comforted me. Very efficient.
Swapped forgotten beast stories with a miner. Both of us lied beautifully.
Long chat in the meeting hall. We solved everything except the elves.
Somebody laughed at my joke about carp. I will be telling it forever.
Good conversation is like good ale: rare, and best shared with friends.

bad.text: I argued with Urist about socks and he simply would not concede.
Somebody said my beard was fine. Fine! I will be brooding for weeks.
I tried to make conversation and got a lecture on hauling efficiency.
We argued until the bell rang. I still do not know what about.
A noble talked at me for an hour. Nothing happened, very slowly.
My friend told me to calm down. I am calm! I am VERY calm!

good.text: I saw an engraving of a dwarf defeating a carp. I nearly cried.
There is a masterwork mug in the tavern. I visit it every day.
Admired a statue on the way to work. Arrived late, but happy.
Someone engraved a picture of cheese into the wall. Pure genius.
The craftsmanship in this fortress is improving. Mine included, of course.
I touched a legendary door today. It was very smooth. Very legendary.

bad.text: There is an engraving of an elf in the hallway. Who approved this?
I saw a crooked statue and it ruined my entire afternoon.
Someone engraved a picture of me. They gave me a small beard.
The decorations here are amateur. A goblin could do better. Possibly did.
Saw a badly made mug. A mug! The very soul of a dwarf, botched.
The walls are bare. Not one engraving. It is like living inside a pebble.

good.text: Fought a goblin today and won. He will think twice. Well, he will not think again.
I took a hit and kept swinging. My axe is very proud of me.
Bruises fade, but a good brawl is remembered forever.
I punched a kobold clean out of the fort. Satisfying morning.
Lost a tooth in battle. Found a goblin's tooth. Fair trade.
Combat is just mining, except the rocks fight back.

bad.text: I was attacked by a carp at the well. Again. I am done with water.
My arm is broken and the doctor is busy hauling.
I got stabbed and nobody brought me a crutch. Or ale. Mostly ale.
A goblin hit me with my own shield. Humiliating, frankly.
I am bandaged from beard to boots. The cat laughed at me.
The fight went badly. I would like to rewind time, please, by a day.

good.text: Saw a ghost last night. Very polite. Only moved one chair.
My departed friend visited me last night. We chatted about the old days.
A ghost waved at me. I waved back. Neighborly, I thought.
The ghost in the hall is quieter than most nobles. I approve.
Haunting is just lingering with style. I respect the commitment.
If I am a ghost one day, I will haunt the brewery. Good plan.

bad.text: A ghost threw my mug across the dining hall. Rude, even for the dead.
There is a ghost in my bedroom. I have asked it to leave. Nicely.
Someone forgot to engrave a slab, and now the dead walk the halls.
The ghost keeps moaning about its coffin. Get in line, friend.
I saw a ghost and my beard went white for a moment.
Haunted again. Somebody please carve a memorial before I throw a tantrum.

good.text: My cat sat on me today. I have officially been chosen.
Trained a war dog and it only bit me twice. Progress.
I petted a yak. The yak tolerated it. We are friends now.
The fortress has kittens again. Thirty of them. All perfect.
My pet followed me to work. Best coworker I have ever had.
I tamed a giant cave spider. Well, it did not eat me. Close enough.

bad.text: The cats outnumber us now. They have started holding meetings.
My pet passed away, and I still keep its little bowl by my bed.
A donkey kicked me. I respect it, but I also hate it.
Someone slaughtered my favorite turkey. I will find out who.
There are forty cats in the dining hall and not one of them is mine.
The war dog chewed my sock. My best sock, the left one.

good.text: The caravan came and I bought nothing, but I looked at everything.
Traders brought ale from far away. I tried some. It is acceptable.
Saw the merchants arrive. Wagons, goods, and gossip. Lovely day.
I watched the broker haggle and learned three new insults.
A trader admired my work. I charged him double. He paid.
Caravan season is the best season. Even elves look tolerable from far away.

bad.text: The elves came to trade and complained about our wooden bins.
The merchants left before I could sell them my socks.
Traders brought goods, and nobody hauled a single bin to the depot.
A human told me my mug was quaint. Quaint! It is a masterwork!
The caravan was eaten on the way here. Worst trade ever.
Our broker traded a masterwork for a bag of seeds. I am devastated.

good.text: I have been {adj} about the {about} business lately. Make of that what you will.
The {about} thing? Yes. It left me {adj}. Write that down.
I am {adj} about the {about} matter, and I do not care who knows it.
Cannot stop thinking about {about}. I am {adj}, actually. Surprised me too.
That whole {about} affair made me {adj}. Not every day goes so well.
Ask me about {about} and I will tell you plainly: {adj}. Next question.

bad.text: I am {adj} about the {about} business. Someone should be held accountable.
The {about} thing. That is the complaint. I am {adj}, and that is that.
The {about} situation left me {adj}, and then it got worse.
Do not mention {about} to me. I am still {adj} over it.
All this {about} has left me {adj}. I will be stomping about it for a week.
I tried not to think about {about}. Now I am {adj} and thinking about it.

job.text: So, what is it you actually do around here?
Tell our readers about your work.
What keeps you busy here in {fort}?
How would you describe your trade to a fresh migrant?
What does a typical day look like for you?
The whole fortress wants to know: what is your job?
Some call you the backbone of this fort. What do you actually do?
How do you earn your daily mug of ale?
What would the fort fall apart without, if not you?

mood.text: How are you feeling these days?
How is your mood holding up this {season}?
How would you rate your spirits, one to ten?
How is the fortress agreeing with you?
Our readers worry about you. How are you holding up?

complaint.text: What has been bothering you lately?
If you could change one thing about {fort}, what would it be?
What is the worst part of fortress life right now?
Got any grudges you would like to air?
Anything keeping you up at night?
What would you tell the mayor, if the mayor ever listened?
What is the one thing you would fix, given a pick and a free afternoon?

deity.text: Is there a god you turn to in hard times?
Does religion play a part in your life down here?

kin.text: Family matters. What can you tell us about {kin}?

nokin.text: Is there anyone special in your life?
Do you have kin in the fortress?
Any sweetheart our readers should know about?

last.text: Any final words for our readers?
Anything else you would like to say?
A message for the good dwarves of {fort}?
Last question: any advice for young dwarves?
What should the fortress know before we go to print?
Before you go, any words of wisdom?
What would you say to the next wave of migrants?

job_match.text: Your humble {level} {skill}, at your service. The rocks know my name and fear it.
I am the {prof}. The record says {level} {skill}, and the record is never wrong, unlike the overseer.
Being the {prof} is my calling. My hands were made for it, and the hands are {level}.
The fortress rolls list me as {level} {skill}. I list myself as indispensable.
They made me {prof} because I am the only {level} {skill} who showed up sober.
I am the {prof}. It says {level} {skill} on my door, which I carved myself, badly.
I have been the {prof} since I could hold a mug. Now I am {level} at it, and insufferable.
Some dwarves find their calling. Mine found me and would not leave. Now I am the fort's {level} {skill}.
I am the {prof}, the {level} kind, not the kind who cancels jobs for a nap.
Being {prof} means everyone needs me. Being the {level} {skill} means they are right to.
One trade, one dwarf, done properly. I am the {prof}, and my work is {level}.
Ask anyone who the {level} {skill} is around here. Then ask them to stop interrupting me.

job_mismatch.text: Officially I am the {prof}. Unofficially I am the fort's {level} {skill}, which nobody asked for.
The paperwork says {prof}. My hands say {level} {skill}, and my hands do not lie.
I am meant to be the {prof}, but somehow I became the {level} {skill}. Life underground is strange.
Title: {prof}. Actual talent: {level} {skill}. Please do not tell the overseer.
I was hired as {prof} but spend my days as the {level} {skill}. The pay is the same: ale.
They call me the {prof}. I have never once done it. I am the {level} {skill}, mostly.
Being {prof} is my title, but being the {level} {skill} is clearly my destiny.
Funny story. I arrived as {prof} and turned out to be the {level} {skill}. Losing is fun.
My door says {prof}. My calluses say {level} {skill}. I trust the calluses.
The {prof}? On paper. In practice I am the {level} {skill}, and the paper can grumble.
The overseer thinks I am the {prof}. The overseer also thinks carp are friendly. I am the {level} {skill}.
Nominally the {prof}. Practically the {level} {skill}. Emotionally, a dwarf who wants ale.

skill2_good.text: I also moonlight as the fort's {skill2}, and I am frankly excellent at it.
On rest days I am the {skill2}. Dwarves line up around the corridor for it.
And do not forget my work as {skill2}, admired across three caverns.
Plus I am a talented {skill2}. Ask anyone, or do not, and I will tell you.
My side trade as {skill2}? Masterful, they say. I say it more often.
When nobody is watching, I am a gifted {skill2}. When they are watching, too.
Also, I make a fine {skill2}. My mother always said so, loudly.

skill2_bad.text: I also try my hand as {skill2}. The results are under investigation.
Sometimes I am the backup {skill2}. We do not talk about those days.
I dabble as {skill2}, which is how the last workshop fire started.
My efforts as {skill2} are improving, in that they have stopped exploding.
I have been asked to stop working as {skill2}. By the mayor. In writing.
I am a hopeful {skill2}. Hope is doing most of the work, frankly.
I took up the {skill2}'s trade recently. Even the cats avoid me now.

mood_ecstatic.text: Never better. I could hug an elf, and I will not, but I could.
I am overflowing with joy, like a well someone forgot to stop pumping.
Wonderful! Even the hauling is starting to feel like a privilege.
Splendid, truly. If I were any happier I would have to file a report.
Ecstatic. I whistled on the stairs today. Nobody has ever whistled on those stairs.
Over the moon, which is saying a lot, since I do not trust the sky.
I am so happy my beard has started curling all by itself.

mood_happy.text: Pretty good, actually. The ale is cold and the walls are smooth.
Happy enough. Nobody has thrown a tantrum near me in days.
Good! I had a decent meal and nothing tried to eat me.
I am doing well. The fort has its faults, but they are mostly downstairs.
Cheerful, I would say. I hummed while working. Badly, but with feeling.
Life is good in {fort}. I would not trade it for a whole elf forest.

mood_content.text: Fine. Not great, not terrible. Rather like a plump helmet, really.
I am content. Content is the most a dwarf should ever admit to a reporter.
Cannot complain. Well, I can, but I am saving it for later.
Steady as bedrock. Nothing to report, which is exactly how I like it.
Middling. I have had better days and I have seen worse goblins.
Alright. I have a bed, a mug, and most of my teeth.

mood_stressed.text: A bit frayed, honestly. Like an old sock. Like all of my socks.
Not great. I have been snapping at the cats, and they snap back.
Stressed. The fort keeps asking things of me and offering nothing but more hauling.
I have been better. I have also been worse, but that was during the siege.
Tense. I clench my jaw so hard I have bitten through two mugs.
Rattled. Something always goes wrong, and it usually goes wrong right next to me.

mood_very_stressed.text: Terrible. I have started talking to the walls, and the walls have started agreeing.
Very bad. If one more dwarf asks me to haul, I will throw them in the river.
Awful. I can feel a tantrum building, like magma behind a thin wall.
Miserable. Even my ale tastes of disappointment lately, and that is a first.
I am not well. I cried in the dining hall and nobody even looked up.
Frayed to the last thread. Please print that I am fine. I am not fine.

mood_breaking.text: I am about to throw a mug at someone. Possibly you. Keep writing.
Breaking. I have been eyeing the furniture, and the furniture knows it.
Do not stand near me. I am one bad thought away from punching a statue.
I am cracking like cheap stone. Someone fetch ale, or a very sturdy door.
Near the edge. Literally, I have been standing near the chasm a lot lately.
Losing is fun, they say, usually right before something terrible. I am the something.

deity.text: I follow {deity}. We do not talk much, but we understand each other.
{deity}, of course. The only god who has never once asked me to haul.
I pray to {deity} whenever there is a cave-in, which around here is weekly.
{deity} watches over me. Probably watched me fall down the stairs, too.
Faith in {deity} gets me through sieges, and through the cooking.
I engraved {deity} on my bedroom wall. It came out looking a bit like a carp.
{deity} is mighty and wise and, as far as I can tell, quite fond of ale.
I keep a little shrine to {deity} right next to my sock drawer.
When the forgotten beast came, I prayed to {deity}. It ate someone else. Prayer works.
{deity} has my devotion. The mayor merely has my patience, and only barely.
I sing hymns to {deity} while I work. My coworkers pray for silence.
I trust {deity}. I do not trust elves, rivers, or anything with feathers.
Ask {deity} yourself. Actually, do not. I am the one with the connection.

kin_alive.text: My {rel}, {kin}, is doing well. We share a love of ale and old grudges.
{kin}? Lovely. Snores like a cave-in, but lovely.
I see my {rel} at dinner most nights. {kin} always steals my plump helmet.
{kin} and I are close. Close enough to argue about socks every week.
My {rel} thinks I work too hard. {kin} has clearly never watched me work.
{kin} is proud of me, I think. Hard to tell underneath all that beard.
Ah, {kin}. Once fought a carp barehanded. Lost, but with tremendous style.
I would lift a mountain for {kin}. Not a big mountain. A medium one.
My {rel}? Fine, fine. {kin} sends regards and asks whether you brought ale.
We do not always see eye to eye, {kin} and I, but blood is thicker than ale. Barely.
{kin} keeps me honest. Somebody has to, and the overseer stopped trying.

kin_dead.text: {kin} is gone now. I still pour a second mug every year on their name day.
My {rel}, {kin}, rests in the tombs. Lovely slab. I picked the stone myself.
I miss {kin}. They would have hated this interview, which makes me smile.
{kin} passed on, but I swear I still hear them complaining about elves.
Lost {kin} some time back. I keep their mug, and nobody else may drink from it.
{kin} died as they lived: mid-argument. I would expect nothing less.
Gone, my {rel}. But if a ghost ever tidies my socks, I will know it is {kin}.
I think of {kin} whenever the ale is good. So, rarely, but fondly.
{kin} is with the gods now. I hope, for everyone's sake, the gods have a brewery.

nokin.text: No family here. I am married to my work, and my work is mostly rocks.
Family? I have a cat who tolerates me. That is close enough.
Nobody yet. The migrant waves keep bringing me all the wrong dwarves.
Single, and I like it that way. More ale for me.
I am still looking. Must love rocks, ale, and long silences.
My family is the fortress. Unfortunately, the fortress is mostly idiots.
No kin to speak of. I have a grudge, though, and I keep it well fed.
Not a soul. If you know a dwarf with a good beard and low standards, send them over.
My kin stayed in the mountainhomes. They would write, if any of them could write.
Family is overrated. Socks, on the other hand, never let you down. Except when they do.
I am courting a statue in the meeting hall. It has not said no yet.

signoff.text: Strike the earth, and do not forget to look out for carp.
Never trust an elf, a river, or a noble who smiles at you.
Drink your ale before someone hauls it away to a stockpile.
Losing is fun. Winning is also fun. Just do not do either near magma.
Keep your socks dry and your grudges warm.
If you see a forgotten beast, no you did not. Walk the other way.
Respect the cats. They outnumber us now, and they know it.
Smooth your walls, engrave your floors, and never dig upward without a plan.
Eat your plump helmets. They are good for you, probably.
Do not go outside. The sky is still far too big.
If you feel a strange mood coming on, grab every bone and shell you can find.
Never, ever let a noble design your dining hall.
Whatever you do, do not dig through the aquifer on a whim.
Bury your dead, people. Ghosts make terrible roommates.
Be kind to the haulers. Sooner or later, you will be one.
A mug in the hand is worth two in the stockpile.
Keep an axe by the door and a barrel of ale by the bed.
Wave politely at the caravan, then count your bins.
Remember: water is for wells and carp, not for drinking.
Love your fortress, even when it is on fire. Especially then.
Tantrums are temporary. Broken furniture, sadly, is forever. Choose wisely.
Never pet a cat in a hurry. Never hurry, period. Dwarves do not hurry.
If the goblins come, stand behind the militia. That is what they are for.
Look after your beard, and your beard will look after you.
Do not drink anything that glows in the caverns. I learned that one the hard way.
Every mug you make is a promise to the future. So make good mugs.
Stay out of the miasma, stay out of trouble, and stay in the tavern.
Long live {fort}, and may its lower halls never flood.
Tell the overseer I said hello, and that I would like a bigger bedroom.
Carry a crutch, just in case. Everyone ends up needing one eventually.
Do not feed the carp. Do not look at the carp. Do not think about carp.
If the meeting hall gets loud, relax. That is just dwarven democracy at work.
Read the Herald, and if you cannot read, hold it up and nod wisely.
Somebody please build a proper temple before I have to pray in the latrine again.
Dig deep, but not too deep. You all know what is down there.
Never lend your pick to a noble. You will not see it again.
Admire the engravings. Somebody bled for those, quite possibly literally.
When the magma comes, be somewhere else, preferably upstairs.
Treat your animals well. The war dogs remember everything.
Count your blessings, then count your barrels. The barrels matter more.
Be like granite: solid, dependable, and just slightly cold to the touch.
This {season}, wear two socks on each foot. Trust me on this.
If you ever meet an elf, smile, nod, and hide the wooden furniture.
Good night, {fort}. Mind the stairs, and mind the carp.
Hauling builds character. I have so much character I can barely stand.

decks.text: Our correspondent found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, mid-{job}, and asked the questions the fortress is asking.
{dwarf}, {age}, the fort's {prof}, agreed to talk only if we did not interrupt their {job} duty. We interrupted.
The Herald tracked down {dwarf}, {age}-year-old {prof}, currently on {job} duty and visibly annoyed about it.
Between bouts of '{job}', {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) sat down with the Herald for a frank chat.
We found {dwarf}, {age}, mid-{job}. The {prof} put down the tools, sighed deeply, and answered everything.
This week the Society Pages visits {dwarf}, {prof}, {age}, who was supposed to be on {job} duty.
Pulled away from '{job}' for exactly one mug's worth of time, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, spoke freely.
{dwarf} is {age}, {prof} by trade, and currently assigned to '{job}'. We asked how that is going.
Readers demanded to hear from {dwarf}, {age}. We found the {prof} mid-{job} and simply refused to leave.
In a rare interview, {dwarf}, {prof}, {age}, spoke to the Herald without once stopping the task at hand: {job}.
Our reporter approached {dwarf} ({age}), {prof}, during '{job}', and survived to file this story.
With the '{job}' only half done, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, granted the Herald a few blunt minutes.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was found on {job} duty in {fort} this {season}, and had plenty to say.
We asked {dwarf}, {age}, to pause the '{job}' for a moment. The {prof} declined, then answered anyway.

idle_decks.text: Our correspondent found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, doing absolutely nothing, and asked about absolutely everything.
With no task assigned, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had all the time in the world for the Herald.
We found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, on break in the meeting hall, staring at a wall with great intensity.
{dwarf}, {age}, is officially our {prof} and currently between jobs. The Herald seized the moment.
Caught loitering near the dining hall, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, agreed to an interview over ale.
Idle hands are the Herald's opportunity: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, sat down and spoke freely.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was found wandering {fort} with nothing to do this {season}. Perfect timing.
Unassigned and unbothered, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, granted the Herald a long, lazy interview.
